questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights
questions.stem: Growth of hair in the armpits and pubic area during puberty occurs in
questions.explanation: Hair growth in the armpits and pubic area is a sign of puberty common to both sexes.

questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights
questions.stem: Which of the following is a sign of puberty in girls?
options: Development of breasts and widening of the hips
Breaking of the voice into a deep tone
questions.explanation: At puberty, girls' breasts develop and their hips widen; a beard and a deep voice are signs in boys.

questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights
questions.stem: Which of the following is a sign of puberty in boys?
options: Growth of hair on the face
questions.explanation: Boys begin to grow facial hair (beard and moustache) at puberty.

questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights
questions.stem: AIDS stands for
questions.explanation: AIDS is Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome, the late stage of HIV infection when the immune system is badly weakened.

questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights
questions.stem: Which of the following is a fundamental human right in the Nigerian Constitution?
options: Right to be obeyed by everybody
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution guarantees fundamental rights such as the right to life, dignity, personal liberty and freedom of expression.

questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights
questions.stem: The body changes that take place during puberty are brought about mainly by
questions.explanation: Hormones released by glands in the body trigger the growth and changes seen at puberty.

questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights
questions.stem: During puberty, bathing at least twice a day is important mainly because
options: the skin stops producing sweat and needs to be kept moist
the hair stops growing and must be kept clean to recover
sweat glands become more active and can cause body odour
the body no longer needs water from food and drinks taken
questions.explanation: At puberty sweat glands become more active, so regular bathing helps to prevent body odour and skin infections.

questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights
questions.stem: During menstruation, a girl should change her sanitary pad regularly in order to
options: make the period last longer than it normally would
questions.explanation: Changing pads regularly keeps the body clean and prevents germs from multiplying and causing infections or odour.

questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights
questions.stem: Which of the following is a need of adolescents?
options: Correct information and guidance from trusted adults
Freedom to do whatever their friends say
questions.explanation: Adolescents need accurate information, guidance and support from parents, teachers and counsellors to cope with changes and make good choices.

questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights
questions.stem: Which of the following is a common sign of a sexually transmitted infection?
options: Itching of the scalp after swimming
Unusual discharge or sores in the genital area
questions.explanation: STIs commonly show as unusual discharge, sores, pain or itching in the genital area, and anyone with such signs should see a health worker.

questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights
questions.stem: HIV weakens the body mainly by attacking the
options: digestive juices of the stomach and gut
bones and joints of the limbs
questions.explanation: HIV destroys white blood cells that defend the body against infection, so the body becomes open to other diseases.

questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights
questions.stem: Which of the following activities does NOT spread HIV?
options: Passing from an infected mother to her baby
Shaking hands with an infected person
questions.explanation: HIV is not spread by casual contact such as handshakes; it spreads through infected blood, unprotected sexual contact and from mother to child.

questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights
questions.stem: The only reliable way for a person to know his or her HIV status is to
options: look at his or her body weight
take an HIV test at a health facility
questions.explanation: Many people with HIV look healthy, so only a test can show whether a person is infected.

questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights
questions.stem: Which is the BEST way an adolescent can handle pressure from friends to try drugs?
options: Say no firmly and seek help from a trusted adult
Try the drug once to please the friends
Join the friends and hide from parents
Keep the matter secret from everyone
questions.explanation: Saying no firmly and talking to a parent, teacher or counsellor protects the adolescent from harm.

questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights
questions.stem: The hormone mainly responsible for the development of male characteristics at puberty is
questions.explanation: Testosterone, produced by the testes, causes changes such as a deeper voice, facial hair and muscle growth in boys.

questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights
questions.stem: A 10-year-old girl is made to hawk on the streets during school hours. Which rights of the child are being violated?
options: The right to vote and be voted for in elections
The right to education and protection from exploitation
The right to marry at any age chosen by her own parents
The right to own land and inherit family property
questions.explanation: Children have a right to education and to protection from child labour and exploitation under the Child's Rights Act.

questions.topic: Family Needs, Goals and Standards
questions.stem: Which of the following is a NEED for a JSS student?
questions.explanation: A school uniform is necessary for attending school, while the others are luxuries or wants.

questions.topic: Family Needs, Goals and Standards
questions.stem: Mrs Eze plans to buy foodstuff for the family for the coming week. This is an example of a
questions.explanation: A goal to be achieved within a short time, such as days or weeks, is a short-term goal.

questions.topic: Family Needs, Goals and Standards
questions.stem: Love, affection and a sense of belonging are examples of
questions.explanation: Emotional needs are needs of the mind and feelings, such as love, security and acceptance.

questions.topic: Family Needs, Goals and Standards
questions.stem: Going to church or mosque meets a family's
questions.explanation: Worship and religious practice meet spiritual needs.

questions.topic: Family Needs, Goals and Standards
questions.stem: Which of the following can cause the needs of families to differ?
questions.explanation: Larger families need more food, space and money, so needs vary with family size, income and age of members.

questions.topic: Family Needs, Goals and Standards
questions.stem: Family standards should be
questions.explanation: Standards that are realistic fit the family's resources, so the family can meet them and feel satisfied.

questions.topic: Family Needs, Goals and Standards
questions.stem: A family saves part of its income every month to pay school fees next term. This shows that the family
options: has no goals and simply keeps money for emergencies
does not need a budget because its income is steady each month
spends money without planning for the months ahead
uses its goals to guide the management of its resources
questions.explanation: Setting a goal (paying fees) and saving towards it shows the family is using goals to plan how resources are used.

questions.topic: Family Needs, Goals and Standards
questions.stem: When money is limited, a family should FIRST spend on
options: basic needs such as food and shelter
questions.explanation: Needs must be met before wants, so food, shelter, health and education come first.

questions.topic: Family Needs, Goals and Standards
questions.stem: Standards that are set by society and accepted by most people are called
questions.explanation: Conventional standards are general rules of society; flexible standards are adjusted by a family to suit its own situation.

questions.topic: Family Needs, Goals and Standards
questions.stem: Goals that are achieved step by step to help reach a long-term goal are called
questions.explanation: Intermediate goals are stepping stones; for example, saving each year is an intermediate goal towards building a house.

questions.topic: Family Needs, Goals and Standards
questions.stem: A family earns ₦200,000 a month. It spends ₦50,000 on rent, ₦80,000 on food and ₦30,000 on transport, and saves the rest. What percentage of its income does it save?

questions.topic: Resources and Decision Making
questions.stem: Resources can be defined as
options: the means available to a family for achieving its goals
the wants of the children only, as listed by parents
the decisions a family regrets after spending money
the problems that a family faces in its daily living
questions.explanation: Resources are anything a family can use, such as money, time, skills and equipment, to reach its goals.

questions.topic: Resources and Decision Making
questions.stem: A plan showing how a person intends to spend his or her time on different activities is called a
questions.explanation: A time plan or schedule helps a person to use time wisely.

questions.topic: Resources and Decision Making
questions.stem: A plan for spending income over a period is called a
questions.explanation: A budget sets out expected income and how it will be spent and saved.

questions.topic: Resources and Decision Making
questions.stem: Which of the following is a good way of managing money?
options: Preparing a budget and following it
Buying anything one sees in the market
Spending all one's money on the first day
questions.explanation: A budget helps a person spend according to needs and plans and avoid waste.

questions.topic: Resources and Decision Making
questions.stem: Sitting down while ironing and keeping tools within easy reach help a homemaker to conserve
questions.explanation: Good work methods reduce unnecessary movement and tiredness, which conserves the homemaker's energy.

questions.topic: Resources and Decision Making
questions.stem: The last step in decision making is
options: identifying the problem to be solved
evaluating the result of the decision
listing the alternatives and their costs
questions.explanation: After acting on a decision, a person should evaluate it to see whether it solved the problem and learn from it.

questions.topic: Resources and Decision Making
questions.stem: Deciding together as a family where to spend the Christmas holiday is an example of a
questions.explanation: A decision taken by family members together and affecting all of them is a family or group decision.

questions.topic: Resources and Decision Making
questions.stem: Chidi has 3 hours after school. He spends 1 hour 30 minutes on homework and 45 minutes on house chores. How many minutes does he have left for leisure?
questions.explanation: 3 hours = 180 minutes; 180 - 90 - 45 = 45 minutes.

questions.topic: Resources and Decision Making
questions.stem: Spending money meant for school fees to buy an expensive phone is an example of
options: a community resource that is shared by all the family members
setting realistic standards for the whole family
a poor decision based on wants rather than needs
good resource management by a careful household
questions.explanation: School fees are a need, while an expensive phone is a want, so the decision wastes resources meant for an important goal.

questions.topic: Resources and Decision Making
questions.stem: A mother uses her sewing skill to make the children's clothes instead of buying them. This shows that resources can be
options: used only once in a family
questions.explanation: Her skill (a human resource) replaces money (a material resource), showing that one resource can be used in place of another.

questions.topic: Resources and Decision Making
questions.stem: Before choosing a secondary school, Musa listed the advantages and disadvantages of three schools. Which step in decision making was he carrying out?
questions.explanation: Weighing the good and bad points of each possible choice is the step of considering the alternatives.

questions.topic: Consumer Challenges and Rights
questions.stem: The right of a consumer to choose from a variety of goods at fair prices is the
questions.explanation: The right to choose means consumers can select among different products and sellers at competitive prices.

questions.topic: Consumer Challenges and Rights
questions.stem: Which of the following is a responsibility of a good consumer?
options: Buying without asking for a receipt
Reading labels and checking expiry dates before buying
Buying goods from anyone without checking
questions.explanation: Consumers have responsibilities as well as rights; reading labels and checking dates help them avoid harmful products.

questions.topic: Consumer Challenges and Rights
questions.stem: The right of a consumer to complain and have the complaint listened to is the
questions.explanation: The right to be heard means consumers' views and complaints must be considered by sellers, producers and government.

questions.topic: Consumer Challenges and Rights
questions.stem: Listening to radio programmes that teach people how to detect fake products helps consumers to enjoy the right to
questions.explanation: Consumer education gives people the knowledge they need to make informed choices and protect themselves.

questions.topic: Consumer Challenges and Rights
questions.stem: A consumer who receives a refund for a faulty electric iron is enjoying the right to
questions.explanation: Redress means the consumer is compensated, through a refund, repair or replacement, for a faulty product or poor service.

questions.topic: Consumer Challenges and Rights
questions.stem: A trader who uses an adjusted measuring tin to sell rice so that buyers get less than they pay for is guilty of
questions.explanation: Using tampered measures cheats buyers by giving them less quantity than they paid for.

questions.topic: Consumer Challenges and Rights
questions.stem: Adding sand to garri to increase its weight before sale is an example of
questions.explanation: Adulteration is adding inferior or harmful substances to a product, which cheats and endangers consumers.

questions.topic: Consumer Challenges and Rights
questions.stem: An advertisement claiming that a cream will change a person's skin colour completely in three days is an example of
questions.explanation: Advertisements that make false or exaggerated claims mislead consumers into buying.

questions.topic: Consumer Challenges and Rights
questions.stem: Traders who keep large stocks of goods away from the market to create scarcity and raise prices are
questions.explanation: Hoarding causes artificial scarcity and high prices, which is a major challenge for consumers.

questions.topic: Consumer Challenges and Rights
questions.stem: A consumer should keep the receipt of a product bought because it
options: is proof of purchase needed when seeking redress
makes the product last longer than the stated period
is used to advertise the product
increases the price of the product
questions.explanation: A receipt proves where, when and for how much the product was bought, which the seller or an agency needs before giving redress.

questions.topic: Consumer Challenges and Rights
questions.stem: A written promise by a manufacturer to repair or replace a product that develops a fault within a stated period is called a
questions.explanation: A guarantee or warranty protects the consumer if the product fails within the stated period.

questions.topic: Consumer Challenges and Rights
questions.stem: After complaining to the seller, the manufacturer and a consumer protection agency without success, the LAST option for a consumer seeking redress is to
options: take the matter to a court of law
questions.explanation: Going to court is the final legal step for redress when other options have failed.

questions.topic: Child Development and Care
questions.stem: The appearance of a baby's first teeth is called
questions.explanation: Teething is the process by which the milk teeth come through the gums, usually from about six months.

questions.topic: Child Development and Care
questions.stem: Which condition is necessary for a child's emotional development?
options: Being left alone most of the time
questions.explanation: Children develop emotionally when they feel loved, secure and accepted.

questions.topic: Child Development and Care
questions.stem: Play is important to children mainly because it
options: stops them from learning bad habits at school
develops their body, mind and social skills
makes them lazy but gives parents time to rest
is a way of wasting time that children must avoid
questions.explanation: Through play, children exercise their muscles, learn to think and solve problems, and learn to relate with others.

questions.topic: Child Development and Care
questions.stem: The gradual introduction of other foods to a baby alongside breast milk is called
questions.explanation: Weaning starts at about six months when the baby needs more nutrients than breast milk alone provides.

questions.topic: Child Development and Care
questions.stem: Children can be protected from malaria by
options: drinking cold water mixed with lime juice before bed
staying in the sun for some time after each meal
eating more sweets and fruits during the rainy season
questions.explanation: Treated nets prevent mosquitoes, which carry malaria parasites, from biting children at night.

questions.topic: Child Development and Care
questions.stem: To prevent accidents at home, medicines and kerosene should be
options: kept out of the reach of children
questions.explanation: Children may swallow medicines or kerosene by mistake, so these must be stored safely out of reach.

questions.topic: Child Development and Care
questions.stem: The stage of child development from conception to birth is called the
questions.explanation: The prenatal stage is the period of growth of the baby in the mother's womb.

questions.topic: Child Development and Care
questions.stem: The stage of a child's life from about one to three years, when the child learns to walk and talk, is called the
questions.explanation: Toddlers are children of about one to three years who are learning to walk steadily and talk.

questions.topic: Child Development and Care
questions.stem: Most babies begin to walk without support at about
questions.explanation: Many babies take their first steps around 12 months, though the age varies from child to child.

questions.topic: Child Development and Care
questions.stem: Which factor that influences child development is passed from parents to the child?
questions.explanation: Heredity is the passing of traits such as height and skin colour from parents to children through genes.

questions.topic: Child Development and Care
questions.stem: Before bathing a baby, the temperature of the water should be tested with the
questions.explanation: The elbow is more sensitive to heat than the hand, so it shows whether the water is safely warm.

questions.topic: Child Development and Care
questions.stem: Which vaccine protects children against polio?
questions.explanation: OPV is given by mouth as drops to protect against poliomyelitis.

questions.topic: Child Development and Care
questions.stem: A child who is very thin, with wrinkled skin like an old person, because of a severe lack of food, is suffering from
questions.explanation: Marasmus is caused by a severe lack of food energy and protein, making the child extremely thin and wasted.

questions.topic: Child Development and Care
questions.stem: In Nigeria's routine immunisation schedule, the first dose of the vaccine that protects against measles is given at about
questions.explanation: The first dose is given at about nine months, when protection from the mother's antibodies has fallen, and a second dose at about 15 months. Since 2025 Nigeria has been using the combined measles-rubella (MR) vaccine.

questions.topic: Child Development and Care
questions.stem: The card used at the clinic to record a child's weight at each visit and the vaccines received is the
options: school report card for nursery pupils
national identity card of the mother
questions.explanation: The growth chart shows whether the child is gaining weight normally and keeps the immunisation record.

questions.topic: Child Development and Care
questions.stem: Which shows the correct order of the stages of child development?
questions.explanation: A child develops in the womb (prenatal), then as an infant, a toddler and a pre-school child before school age.

questions.topic: Production of Clothing, Household Articles and Crafts
questions.stem: Which tool is used to mark lines on fabric before cutting?
questions.explanation: Tailor's chalk makes clear marks on fabric that can be brushed off later.

questions.topic: Production of Clothing, Household Articles and Crafts
questions.stem: Pins are used in sewing to
options: cut fabric along the marked lines
measure the body for a new garment
hold fabric pieces together before stitching
questions.explanation: Pins hold fabric or patterns in place temporarily until the fabric is tacked or stitched.

questions.topic: Production of Clothing, Household Articles and Crafts
questions.stem: A thick padded article used to hold hot pots in the kitchen is called a
questions.explanation: A pot holder or oven glove protects the hands from burns when handling hot pots.

questions.topic: Production of Clothing, Household Articles and Crafts
questions.stem: Decorating fabric with coloured threads stitched into designs is called
questions.explanation: Embroidery uses decorative stitches in coloured threads to create patterns on fabric.

questions.topic: Production of Clothing, Household Articles and Crafts
questions.stem: A hooked tool used to loop yarn into lace, caps and bags is called a
questions.explanation: Crochet uses a single hooked tool to make loops of yarn into fabric.

questions.topic: Production of Clothing, Household Articles and Crafts
questions.stem: Making a sweater by looping yarn with two long needles is called
questions.explanation: Knitting forms rows of interlocking loops using two (or more) knitting needles.

questions.topic: Production of Clothing, Household Articles and Crafts
questions.stem: In batik, hot wax is applied to parts of a fabric in order to
options: prevent the dye from reaching those parts
questions.explanation: The wax resists the dye, so waxed areas stay their original colour and form the pattern.

questions.topic: Production of Clothing, Household Articles and Crafts
questions.stem: A long, temporary stitch used to hold fabric in place before permanent stitching is called
questions.explanation: Tacking stitches are large and easy to remove after the permanent stitching is done.

questions.topic: Production of Clothing, Household Articles and Crafts
questions.stem: A student spends ₦600 on materials for each table mat and sells each at ₦1,000. What is her profit on 15 mats?

questions.topic: Production of Clothing, Household Articles and Crafts
questions.stem: In tie-dye, parts of the fabric are tied tightly with thread or rubber bands before dyeing because
options: the threads add colour to the fabric
tying makes the fabric absorb more dye everywhere
the tied parts resist the dye and form patterns
it prevents the fabric from shrinking
questions.explanation: Tightly tied parts do not take in the dye, so they remain lighter and create the patterns.

questions.topic: Production of Clothing, Household Articles and Crafts
questions.stem: A small slanting stitch used to hold a folded edge such as the hem of a skirt in place is the
questions.explanation: Hemming stitches are small, slanting and almost invisible on the right side of the fabric.

questions.topic: Production of Clothing, Household Articles and Crafts
questions.stem: Which fabric is MOST suitable for making an oven glove?
questions.explanation: Thick cotton does not melt and protects the hand from heat, while synthetic fabrics such as nylon can melt and cause burns.

questions.topic: Care of Family Clothing and Household Linen
questions.stem: Which of the following is a table linen?
questions.explanation: Tablecloths and table napkins are table linen; pillowcases and bedspreads are bed linen and towels are bathroom linen.

questions.topic: Care of Family Clothing and Household Linen
questions.stem: Replacing a lost button on a shirt promptly is part of
questions.explanation: Mending includes sewing on buttons, fixing hooks and repairing seams so that clothes last longer.

questions.topic: Care of Family Clothing and Household Linen
questions.stem: Clothes such as suits and dresses are best stored by
options: folding them tightly in a damp bag
hanging them on hangers in a wardrobe
questions.explanation: Hanging keeps garments free from creases and lets air circulate around them.

questions.topic: Care of Family Clothing and Household Linen
questions.stem: Bath towels are best made from cotton terry cloth mainly because it is
questions.explanation: Terry cloth has many loops of cotton yarn that soak up water well.

questions.topic: Care of Family Clothing and Household Linen
questions.stem: A fabric whose colour does not run when it is washed is said to be
questions.explanation: Colourfast fabrics keep their colour during washing, so they do not stain other items.

questions.topic: Care of Family Clothing and Household Linen
questions.stem: Before washing household linen, the items should first be
questions.explanation: Sorting prevents coloured items from staining white ones and allows each fabric to be washed correctly.

questions.topic: Care of Family Clothing and Household Linen
questions.stem: Stains should be removed while they are still fresh because
options: old stains disappear by themselves after several washes
fresh stains improve the fabric once they have dried
fresh stains cannot be seen until the fabric is ironed
old stains set into the fabric and are harder to remove
questions.explanation: The longer a stain stays, the more firmly it sets into the fibres.

questions.topic: Care of Family Clothing and Household Linen
questions.stem: Which fabric should be ironed with a cool iron?
questions.explanation: Nylon is a synthetic fibre that melts or shines at high temperatures, so it needs a cool iron; cotton and linen take high heat.

questions.topic: Care of Family Clothing and Household Linen
questions.stem: Black spots on towels that were folded and stored while still damp are caused by
questions.explanation: Mildew is a fungus that grows on damp fabrics, leaving dark spots and a musty smell.

questions.topic: Care of Family Clothing and Household Linen
questions.stem: A seam on a pair of trousers that has come apart is best repaired by
questions.explanation: Re-sewing along the original seam line is the simple and correct repair for an opened seam.

questions.topic: Care of Family Clothing and Household Linen
questions.stem: Using two or more sets of bed sheets in rotation helps to
options: stop the need to wash them
make them wear evenly and last longer
make them wear out faster than single sheets
questions.explanation: Rotating linen spreads the wear over several sets so that none wears out too quickly.

questions.topic: Care of Family Clothing and Household Linen
questions.stem: A homemaker wants to buy new bed sheets. What should she check FIRST to avoid waste?
options: The type of floor in the room
questions.explanation: Sheets must fit the bed; buying the wrong size wastes money however good the fabric.

questions.topic: Basic Pattern Drafting Techniques and Fashion Designing
questions.stem: A drawing that shows the style of a garment before it is made is called a
questions.explanation: A fashion sketch shows what the finished garment will look like.

questions.topic: Basic Pattern Drafting Techniques and Fashion Designing
questions.stem: Which paper is commonly used for drafting patterns?
questions.explanation: Brown paper or pattern paper is strong enough to draft on and reuse.

questions.topic: Basic Pattern Drafting Techniques and Fashion Designing
questions.stem: Which tool is used to draw long straight lines when drafting a pattern?
questions.explanation: A metre rule (long ruler) helps to draw straight lines such as centre front and hem lines.

questions.topic: Basic Pattern Drafting Techniques and Fashion Designing
questions.stem: The measurement taken from the nape of the neck down to the waist at the back is the
questions.explanation: Nape to waist gives the back length of a bodice.

questions.topic: Basic Pattern Drafting Techniques and Fashion Designing
questions.stem: Body measurements should be taken over
options: light clothing, with the tape neither too tight nor too loose
a different person's body of about the same size, height and shape
bare skin pulled very tightly to show the exact body shape
thick coats and sweaters so that the garment will be roomy
questions.explanation: Measuring over light clothing with a comfortable tape gives accurate measurements.

questions.topic: Basic Pattern Drafting Techniques and Fashion Designing
questions.stem: Extra fabric added outside the fitting line to allow pieces to be joined is called the
questions.explanation: Seam allowance is the margin of fabric beyond the stitching line, usually about 1.5 cm.

questions.topic: Basic Pattern Drafting Techniques and Fashion Designing
questions.stem: Small marks cut or drawn on the edges of pattern pieces to show where they should be matched are called
questions.explanation: Notches help to join pattern pieces accurately at the right points.

questions.topic: Basic Pattern Drafting Techniques and Fashion Designing
questions.stem: A line marked 'place on fold' on a pattern piece means that the piece should be
options: placed on the folded edge of the fabric
placed on the selvedge only, away from the fold
questions.explanation: Placing on the fold produces one symmetrical piece twice the width of the pattern.

questions.topic: Basic Pattern Drafting Techniques and Fashion Designing
questions.stem: A basic pattern without style details, from which other styles are developed, is called a
questions.explanation: The block is the foundation pattern made from body measurements and adapted for different designs.

questions.topic: Basic Pattern Drafting Techniques and Fashion Designing
questions.stem: The grain line arrow on a pattern piece should be placed
options: across the fabric at an angle
questions.explanation: Placing the grain line parallel to the selvedge ensures that the garment hangs well and does not twist.

questions.topic: Basic Pattern Drafting Techniques and Fashion Designing
questions.stem: Vertical lines in a dress design tend to make the wearer look
questions.explanation: Vertical lines lead the eye up and down, creating an impression of height and slimness.

questions.topic: Basic Pattern Drafting Techniques and Fashion Designing
questions.stem: A skirt pattern is drafted with a waist-to-knee length of 60 cm. A hem allowance of 4 cm and a waist seam allowance of 1.5 cm are added. What is the cutting length?
questions.explanation: Cutting length = 60 + 4 + 1.5 = 65.5 cm.

questions.topic: Textiles: Properties, Production, Uses and Care
questions.stem: Silk is obtained from
options: the seed of the cotton plant
questions.explanation: Silkworms spin cocoons of fine silk filament, which is unwound and made into thread.

questions.topic: Textiles: Properties, Production, Uses and Care
questions.stem: Fibres obtained from plants and animals are called
questions.explanation: Cotton, linen, silk and wool come from plants or animals, so they are natural fibres.

questions.topic: Textiles: Properties, Production, Uses and Care
questions.stem: The firm woven edge along the length of a fabric that does not fray is called the
questions.explanation: The selvedge is the self-finished edge of woven fabric.

questions.topic: Textiles: Properties, Production, Uses and Care
questions.stem: Which of the following is an importance of textiles?
options: They are used as cooking fuel in many homes
They are used to build roads and bridges
They are eaten as food in most parts of Nigeria
They provide clothing that protects the body
questions.explanation: Textiles are used for clothing, household articles and industry, protecting the body and providing jobs.

questions.topic: Textiles: Properties, Production, Uses and Care
questions.stem: Aso-oke is a hand-woven fabric associated mainly with the
questions.explanation: Aso-oke is woven on traditional looms in south-western Nigeria and is worn by the Yoruba for special occasions.

questions.topic: Textiles: Properties, Production, Uses and Care
questions.stem: In weaving, the threads that run across the width of the fabric are called the
questions.explanation: Weft threads pass across from selvedge to selvedge, interlacing with the lengthwise warp threads.

questions.topic: Textiles: Properties, Production, Uses and Care
questions.stem: Linen fabric is obtained from the
questions.explanation: Linen is made from fibres in the stem of the flax plant.

questions.topic: Textiles: Properties, Production, Uses and Care
questions.stem: Which group contains only synthetic fibres?
questions.explanation: Polyester, nylon and acrylic are made from chemicals derived from petroleum; cotton, silk, wool and linen are natural.

questions.topic: Textiles: Properties, Production, Uses and Care
questions.stem: Cotton is suitable for clothing in hot weather mainly because it
options: melts in the sun and feels soft
questions.explanation: Cotton is absorbent and allows air to pass, so it keeps the body cool.

questions.topic: Textiles: Properties, Production, Uses and Care
questions.stem: One property of nylon is that it
options: shrinks greatly in hot water like wool
questions.explanation: Nylon absorbs little water, so it dries quickly; it is also strong and elastic.

questions.topic: Textiles: Properties, Production, Uses and Care
questions.stem: Silk garments are best washed by
options: scrubbing hard with a brush on a washing board
boiling in hot water with strong laundry soap
squeezing gently in lukewarm water with mild soap
soaking in bleach overnight and drying in the hot sun
questions.explanation: Silk is delicate, so gentle washing in lukewarm water with mild soap prevents damage.

questions.topic: Textiles: Properties, Production, Uses and Care
questions.stem: One reason for studying textiles is to
options: make wise choices when buying and caring for fabrics
grow cotton in the classroom and spin it into fine thread
learn how to drive machines in textile factories
learn how to mix the chemicals used in making soap
questions.explanation: Knowing fibre properties helps people choose suitable fabrics and care for them correctly.

questions.topic: Textiles: Properties, Production, Uses and Care
questions.stem: When a fibre is burnt, it gives a smell like burning hair and leaves a black, crushable ash. The fibre is most likely
questions.explanation: Animal fibres such as wool contain protein and smell like burning hair; cotton and linen smell like burning paper and nylon melts.

questions.topic: Textiles: Properties, Production, Uses and Care
questions.stem: In a plain weave, each weft thread passes
options: only along the selvedge on both sides of the cloth
over one warp thread and under the next
under all the warp threads in each row
over all the warp threads on the loom
questions.explanation: Plain weave is the simplest weave: one over, one under, alternating in each row, as used in a simple woven table mat.

questions.topic: Textiles: Properties, Production, Uses and Care
questions.stem: Rayon (viscose) is described as a regenerated fibre because it is made from
options: petroleum products only, with no natural materials
silkworm cocoons that are unwound into long threads
wood pulp (cellulose) that is chemically treated
animal hair that is washed, combed and spun
questions.explanation: Rayon is made by dissolving natural cellulose from wood pulp and reforming it into fibres.

questions.topic: Textiles: Properties, Production, Uses and Care
questions.stem: A polyester-cotton blend is popular for school uniforms mainly because it
options: is strong and comfortable to wear
questions.explanation: Blending gives a fabric that is strong, does not crease easily and is still comfortable to wear.

questions.topic: Textiles: Properties, Production, Uses and Care
questions.stem: Which is the correct order of laundering?
options: Sorting, soaking, washing, rinsing, drying, ironing
Ironing, washing, sorting, drying, rinsing, soaking
Drying, rinsing, soaking, sorting, ironing, washing
Washing, ironing, sorting, soaking, rinsing, drying
questions.explanation: Clothes are sorted first, soaked to loosen dirt, washed, rinsed free of soap, dried and then ironed.

questions.topic: Sewing Machine and Garment Construction Processes
questions.stem: The three main types of sewing machine are the hand machine, the treadle machine and the
questions.explanation: Sewing machines are operated by hand, by foot (treadle) or by electricity.

questions.topic: Sewing Machine and Garment Construction Processes
questions.stem: The part of the sewing machine that carries the thread through the fabric is the
questions.explanation: The needle pierces the fabric and carries the upper thread through to form stitches with the bobbin thread.

questions.topic: Sewing Machine and Garment Construction Processes
questions.stem: The part of the sewing machine on which the reel of thread is placed is the
questions.explanation: The spool pin holds the reel of upper thread.

questions.topic: Sewing Machine and Garment Construction Processes
questions.stem: Which factor should be considered when buying a sewing machine?
questions.explanation: Spare parts should be easy to get so the machine can be repaired when needed.

questions.topic: Sewing Machine and Garment Construction Processes
questions.stem: Covering the sewing machine after use helps to
questions.explanation: A cover protects the machine from dust, which can clog moving parts.

questions.topic: Sewing Machine and Garment Construction Processes
questions.stem: The part used to change the length of the stitches on a sewing machine is the
questions.explanation: The stitch regulator controls how far the fabric moves for each stitch, which sets the stitch length.

questions.topic: Sewing Machine and Garment Construction Processes
questions.stem: The part of a sewing machine that controls the tightness of the upper thread is the
questions.explanation: The tension discs press on the upper thread so that it forms balanced stitches with the lower thread.

questions.topic: Sewing Machine and Garment Construction Processes
questions.stem: The part of the sewing machine that moves the fabric forward as stitches are made is the
questions.explanation: The feed dog has small teeth below the presser foot that move the fabric along.

questions.topic: Sewing Machine and Garment Construction Processes
questions.stem: The wheel at the right side of the machine that is turned to raise or lower the needle by hand is the
questions.explanation: Turning the hand wheel moves the needle up and down manually.

questions.topic: Sewing Machine and Garment Construction Processes
questions.stem: A piece of fabric stitched to the neckline and turned inside to neaten the raw edge is called a
questions.explanation: A facing finishes edges such as necklines and armholes neatly.

questions.topic: Sewing Machine and Garment Construction Processes
questions.stem: Drawing up fabric into many small folds so that it fits a smaller part, such as the waist of a baby dress, is called
questions.explanation: Gathers are made by pulling up rows of long stitches to control fullness.

questions.topic: Sewing Machine and Garment Construction Processes
questions.stem: The simplest and most commonly used seam is the
questions.explanation: A plain seam is made by stitching two pieces right sides together on the fitting line.

questions.topic: Sewing Machine and Garment Construction Processes
questions.stem: Raw edges of seams are overcast in order to
options: change the colour of the seam
questions.explanation: Overcasting wraps thread over the raw edge, stopping the threads of the fabric from unravelling.

questions.topic: Sewing Machine and Garment Construction Processes
questions.stem: Which fabric is MOST suitable for making a simple baby dress?
questions.explanation: Soft cotton is gentle on a baby's skin, absorbent and easy to wash.

questions.topic: Sewing Machine and Garment Construction Processes
questions.stem: A sewing machine keeps skipping stitches. The MOST likely cause is
options: a clean machine with fresh oil in it
a blunt, bent or wrongly inserted needle
a correctly filled bobbin in its case
too much light in the room for the operator
questions.explanation: A damaged or wrongly placed needle cannot pick up the bobbin thread properly, so stitches are skipped.

questions.topic: Sewing Machine and Garment Construction Processes
questions.stem: The upper thread on a sewing machine keeps breaking while sewing. A likely cause is that the
options: upper thread tension is too tight
questions.explanation: Very tight upper tension puts too much strain on the thread, causing it to break.

questions.topic: Production of Cleaning Agents, Deodorants and Cosmetics
questions.stem: Wood ash mixed with a little water is used traditionally to
options: perfume clothes stored in a box
questions.explanation: Wood ash is slightly rough and alkaline, so it helps to scrub off soot and grease from pots.

questions.topic: Production of Cleaning Agents, Deodorants and Cosmetics
questions.stem: Which of the following is a cosmetic?
questions.explanation: Body lotion is applied to the skin to improve its appearance and feel, so it is a cosmetic.

questions.topic: Production of Cleaning Agents, Deodorants and Cosmetics
questions.stem: Which item is needed to measure ingredients accurately when making pomade?
options: Pair of scissors and a ruler
questions.explanation: Correct measurement of ingredients gives a product of good quality, so scales and measuring spoons are used.

questions.topic: Production of Cleaning Agents, Deodorants and Cosmetics
questions.stem: One advantage of home-made cleaning agents is that they are
options: cheap and made from local materials
questions.explanation: Local materials such as ash, lime and vinegar are cheap and easy to get.

questions.topic: Production of Cleaning Agents, Deodorants and Cosmetics
questions.stem: Nigerian black soap (ose dudu) is made traditionally from
options: caustic soda, coconut oil and scented perfume oil
cement, lime and water boiled together in a clay pot
sugar, flour and groundnut oil boiled together until thick and dark
ash of plantain peels or cocoa pods and palm kernel oil
questions.explanation: The ash supplies the alkali, which reacts with the oil to form soap.

questions.topic: Production of Cleaning Agents, Deodorants and Cosmetics
questions.stem: A mixture of vinegar and water can be used at home to clean
questions.explanation: Vinegar removes smears and stains on glass and leaves it clear.

questions.topic: Production of Cleaning Agents, Deodorants and Cosmetics
questions.stem: Baking soda (bicarbonate of soda) can be used at home to
options: remove odours and clean surfaces such as the inside of a refrigerator
make pomade shiny and give it a pleasant lasting smell when rubbed on the hair
dye fabrics a bright colour without the need for any other chemicals
cook rice faster without water or any other liquid in a closed pot
questions.explanation: Baking soda neutralises smells and is a mild abrasive for cleaning.

questions.topic: Production of Cleaning Agents, Deodorants and Cosmetics
questions.stem: Using skin-lightening creams that contain mercury can cause
options: faster hair growth on the scalp and arms
skin damage and harm to the kidneys
questions.explanation: Mercury is poisonous; it can damage the skin and enter the body to harm the kidneys and nerves.

questions.topic: Production of Cleaning Agents, Deodorants and Cosmetics
questions.stem: Which of the following is a sign that a cosmetic product has expired?
options: It was bought recently from a local shop
It has a clear label with a batch number
It is in a clean, tightly closed container
A change in its smell, colour or texture
questions.explanation: Expired cosmetics often separate, change colour or smell bad, and should not be used.

questions.topic: Production of Cleaning Agents, Deodorants and Cosmetics
questions.stem: Which is a good practice when using cosmetics?
options: Not sharing eye and lip products with others
questions.explanation: Sharing eye and lip products can spread infections from one person to another.

questions.topic: Production of Cleaning Agents, Deodorants and Cosmetics
questions.stem: Home-made floor or wood polish can be prepared by dissolving candle (paraffin) wax in
options: tap water, stirred well until the wax has dissolved
kerosene or turpentine, away from naked flames
palm wine kept warm over a low fire
vinegar heated gently over an open flame
questions.explanation: Wax dissolves in kerosene or turpentine, but these are flammable, so the work must be done away from fire.

questions.topic: Production of Cleaning Agents, Deodorants and Cosmetics
questions.stem: When making home-made pomade, the perfume should be added
options: after the pomade has set hard in the tin
while the mixture is boiling hard
after the melted mixture has cooled slightly
questions.explanation: Adding perfume to a very hot mixture makes it evaporate, so it is added when the mixture has cooled a little.

questions.topic: Production of Cleaning Agents, Deodorants and Cosmetics
questions.stem: An antiperspirant differs from an ordinary deodorant in that an antiperspirant
options: reduces the amount of sweat produced
only adds perfume to the body
questions.explanation: Antiperspirants contain substances that reduce sweating, while deodorants mainly reduce or mask odour.

questions.topic: Production of Cleaning Agents, Deodorants and Cosmetics
questions.stem: When making liquid soap with caustic soda, gloves and goggles should be worn because caustic soda
options: can burn the skin and eyes
questions.explanation: Caustic soda (sodium hydroxide) is strongly alkaline and corrosive, so protective clothing must be worn.

questions.topic: Healthy Feeding and Eating Practice
questions.stem: Chewing food properly before swallowing helps to
questions.explanation: Chewing breaks food into small pieces and mixes it with saliva, which makes digestion easier.

questions.topic: Healthy Feeding and Eating Practice
questions.stem: Talking with food in the mouth can lead to
questions.explanation: Food can go down the windpipe when a person talks while eating, causing choking.

questions.topic: Healthy Feeding and Eating Practice
questions.stem: Taking a small quantity of food into the mouth at a time helps to
questions.explanation: Small mouthfuls are easy to chew and swallow and allow a person to eat at a sensible pace.

questions.topic: Healthy Feeding and Eating Practice
questions.stem: A labourer needs more energy-giving foods than an office worker mainly because he
options: is older than the office worker
is taller and has larger bones
questions.explanation: Heavy physical work uses more energy, so the diet must supply more carbohydrates and fats.

questions.topic: Healthy Feeding and Eating Practice
questions.stem: A student who skips breakfast regularly is likely to
options: have more energy in the morning
find it hard to concentrate in class
questions.explanation: Without breakfast the body and brain lack energy in the morning, which reduces concentration.

questions.topic: Healthy Feeding and Eating Practice
questions.stem: Eating too much salt regularly can lead to
questions.explanation: Excess salt raises blood pressure, which can lead to heart disease and stroke.

questions.topic: Healthy Feeding and Eating Practice
questions.stem: Seasoning cubes added to soups and stews are examples of food additives used as
questions.explanation: Seasoning cubes improve the taste of food, so they are flavour enhancers.

questions.topic: Healthy Feeding and Eating Practice
questions.stem: The BEST way for a consumer to detect additives in packaged food is to
options: shake the package and listen to its contents
look at the price and compare it with others
smell the package before paying for it
read the list of ingredients on the label
questions.explanation: Manufacturers list ingredients, including additives, on the label.

questions.topic: Healthy Feeding and Eating Practice
questions.stem: Hair, stones and insects found in a bag of rice are examples of
questions.explanation: Physical contaminants are foreign objects in food that can cause injury or illness.

questions.topic: Healthy Feeding and Eating Practice
questions.stem: Drug abuse can be defined as
options: drinking clean water instead of taking the tablets that the doctor gave
eating a balanced diet while taking medicine for a short illness
taking drugs without a doctor's prescription or in excessive amounts
taking medicine exactly as prescribed by a qualified doctor or nurse
questions.explanation: Drug abuse is the wrong or excessive use of drugs, often without medical advice.

questions.topic: Healthy Feeding and Eating Practice
questions.stem: Abuse of cough syrup containing codeine can lead to
questions.explanation: Codeine is habit-forming; abusing it causes dependence and harms the brain and other organs.

questions.topic: Healthy Feeding and Eating Practice
questions.stem: A diet lacking vitamin A for a long time can lead to
questions.explanation: Vitamin A is needed for vision in dim light, so its lack causes night blindness.

questions.topic: Healthy Feeding and Eating Practice
questions.stem: Groundnuts and maize that have become mouldy should not be eaten because the mould can produce
options: vitamins, which are destroyed by heat
sugar, which makes the food sweet
extra protein, which upsets the stomach
questions.explanation: Some moulds produce aflatoxins, which can damage the liver and cause cancer.

questions.topic: Healthy Feeding and Eating Practice
questions.stem: Cassava must be properly processed by soaking, fermenting or cooking before eating mainly to
options: remove the poisonous cyanide it contains
remove all its starch and leave only fibre
questions.explanation: Raw cassava contains cyanide compounds; processing removes them and makes the food safe.

questions.topic: Healthy Feeding and Eating Practice
questions.stem: Using formalin to preserve fish sold in the market is dangerous mainly because formalin is
questions.explanation: Formalin is a toxic chemical meant for preserving dead bodies, not food, and it can harm people who eat the fish.

questions.topic: Food Purchasing, Processing, Preservation and Safety
questions.stem: Which of these foods is perishable?
questions.explanation: Fresh tomatoes contain much water and spoil within days, while dried beans, garri and oil keep for a long time.

questions.topic: Food Purchasing, Processing, Preservation and Safety
questions.stem: Food purchasing means
options: buying food items for the family
questions.explanation: Food purchasing is the buying of food, which should be done wisely to get value for money.

questions.topic: Food Purchasing, Processing, Preservation and Safety
questions.stem: Drying okra and pepper in the sun helps to preserve them because it
options: adds germs to the food that improve its taste
increases spoilage enzymes that soften the food
removes the water that germs need to grow
makes the food wet enough to keep for months
questions.explanation: Micro-organisms need water; drying takes it away, so the food keeps longer.

questions.topic: Food Purchasing, Processing, Preservation and Safety
questions.stem: Keeping food in a refrigerator preserves it because the low temperature
options: cooks the food slowly over several hours
slows down the growth of micro-organisms
adds water to the food and keeps it fresh
kills all germs immediately and completely
questions.explanation: Cold temperatures slow the multiplication of germs and the activity of enzymes that spoil food.

questions.topic: Food Purchasing, Processing, Preservation and Safety
questions.stem: In canning, food is heated and sealed in airtight containers in order to
options: kill germs and keep air out
questions.explanation: Heating destroys micro-organisms, and the airtight seal stops new germs from entering.

questions.topic: Food Purchasing, Processing, Preservation and Safety
questions.stem: Mango jam keeps for a long time mainly because the high amount of sugar
questions.explanation: A high sugar concentration draws water out of germs, so they cannot grow.

questions.topic: Food Purchasing, Processing, Preservation and Safety
questions.stem: A family that has no refrigerator should buy perishable foods
options: only when they have already spoilt
in small quantities, enough for a short time
questions.explanation: Without cold storage, perishable foods spoil quickly, so they should be bought in small amounts.

questions.topic: Food Purchasing, Processing, Preservation and Safety
questions.stem: Buying rice in large quantities during the harvest season when it is cheap is wise because
options: it saves money and the rice can be stored well
prices are always higher at harvest
questions.explanation: Rice is non-perishable, so buying in bulk when prices are low saves money.

questions.topic: Food Purchasing, Processing, Preservation and Safety
questions.stem: Soaking maize and leaving it to turn sour to make ogi (pap) is an example of
questions.explanation: Fermentation uses micro-organisms to change the food, giving ogi its sour taste.

questions.topic: Food Purchasing, Processing, Preservation and Safety
questions.stem: Which of the following is a risk factor when buying packaged food?
options: A sealed package with a batch number
A package with no label or registration number
A clean shop with well-arranged shelves
A clear expiry date printed by the manufacturer on the pack
questions.explanation: Unlabelled products may be fake or unsafe because their source and contents cannot be checked.

questions.topic: Food Purchasing, Processing, Preservation and Safety
questions.stem: Preserving vegetables in vinegar is called
questions.explanation: Vinegar is acidic, and the acid prevents the growth of micro-organisms.

questions.topic: Food Purchasing, Processing, Preservation and Safety
questions.stem: Parboiling rice before drying and milling helps to
options: make the rice spoil faster so that it is sold sooner
remove all the nutrients and leave only the bran layer
turn the rice into flour before it reaches the mill
reduce breakage of the grains and keep more nutrients
questions.explanation: Parboiling hardens the grain so it breaks less during milling and drives some nutrients into the grain.

questions.topic: Food Purchasing, Processing, Preservation and Safety
questions.stem: Frozen chicken should be thawed safely by
options: soaking it in hot water for a whole day
leaving it on the kitchen table overnight
keeping it in the refrigerator or in cold water
questions.explanation: Slow thawing in the cold keeps the outside of the meat from warming to temperatures at which germs multiply.

questions.topic: Food Purchasing, Processing, Preservation and Safety
questions.stem: Most food preservation methods work mainly by
options: exposing food to flies and dust
questions.explanation: Micro-organisms need water, warmth and air; preservation methods remove one or more of these.

questions.topic: Food Hygiene and Safety
questions.stem: Why should the fingernails of food handlers be kept short and clean?
options: Germs and dirt can hide under long nails and get into food
Long nails break easily and make handling of knives difficult
Long nails keep food warm and that makes it spoil more quickly
Short nails make it easier to taste the food with the fingers
questions.explanation: Dirt and germs collect under long nails and can contaminate food.

questions.topic: Food Hygiene and Safety
questions.stem: Fruits should be washed before eating in order to remove
questions.explanation: Washing removes dirt, micro-organisms and pesticide residues from the skin of fruits.

questions.topic: Food Hygiene and Safety
questions.stem: Which of the following is a source of food contamination in the kitchen?
options: Boiled water in a clean pot
Clean plates on a dry rack
questions.explanation: Dirty chopping boards carry germs that can pass to food.

questions.topic: Food Hygiene and Safety
questions.stem: Drinking water used for cooking should be
questions.explanation: Boiling or treating water kills germs that cause diseases such as cholera and typhoid.

questions.topic: Food Hygiene and Safety
questions.stem: Which practice prevents contamination when serving food at a party?
options: Using clean serving spoons instead of bare hands
Touching food with hands that have just been wiped on an apron
Tasting from the pot with the same spoon each time
Leaving food uncovered so that guests can see it
questions.explanation: Clean serving utensils prevent germs from the hands getting into the food.

questions.topic: Food Hygiene and Safety
questions.stem: Cholera and typhoid can be spread through
questions.explanation: These diseases are caused by germs that enter the body in contaminated food and water.

questions.topic: Food Hygiene and Safety
questions.stem: A cook who has diarrhoea should
options: stop handling food until he recovers
questions.explanation: A sick food handler can pass germs to food and cause outbreaks of disease.

questions.topic: Food Hygiene and Safety
questions.stem: Milk that smells sour and has curdled has been spoilt mainly by
questions.explanation: Bacteria in milk produce acid, which gives a sour smell and causes curdling.

questions.topic: Food Hygiene and Safety
questions.stem: Germs in cooked food multiply fastest when the food is kept
questions.explanation: Most germs grow quickly at warm temperatures, so cooked food should be kept either hot or cold.

questions.topic: Food Hygiene and Safety
questions.stem: Which of the following are common symptoms of food poisoning?
options: Toothache only, lasting for several days
Itching of the scalp and loss of hair
Sneezing, a runny nose and watery eyes
questions.explanation: Food poisoning affects the stomach and intestines, causing vomiting, diarrhoea and cramps.

questions.topic: Food Hygiene and Safety
questions.stem: A cook with a cut on the hand should cover it with a waterproof dressing mainly to
options: make cooking faster by protecting the sore hand
hide the wound from customers and other workers
prevent germs from the wound getting into food
keep the hand warm and speed up the healing
questions.explanation: Wounds can carry germs, and a waterproof cover keeps them from contaminating the food.

questions.topic: Food Hygiene and Safety
questions.stem: Orange juice left at room temperature for days tastes sour and forms bubbles. This spoilage is caused mainly by
questions.explanation: Yeasts ferment the sugar in juice, producing gas (bubbles) and a sour, alcoholic taste.

questions.topic: Preparation, Packaging and Marketing of Food
questions.stem: Which of the following is a main meal?
options: A cup of zobo and puff-puff
questions.explanation: Pounded yam with egusi soup is a filling meal eaten at a regular mealtime; the others are snacks or drinks.

questions.topic: Preparation, Packaging and Marketing of Food
questions.stem: Akara is made from
options: wheat flour baked in an oven
questions.explanation: Akara is made by frying balls of seasoned, ground beans paste.

questions.topic: Preparation, Packaging and Marketing of Food
questions.stem: Thin slices of unripe plantain fried until crisp are called
questions.explanation: Plantain chips are a popular packaged snack sold across Nigeria.

questions.topic: Preparation, Packaging and Marketing of Food
questions.stem: Kunu is a drink made mainly from
questions.explanation: Kunu is made from grains such as millet or sorghum, often spiced with ginger.

questions.topic: Preparation, Packaging and Marketing of Food
questions.stem: Chin-chin is made mainly from
questions.explanation: Chin-chin dough is made from flour, sugar, fat and sometimes eggs, cut into small pieces and fried.

questions.topic: Preparation, Packaging and Marketing of Food
questions.stem: Moi-moi is cooked by
questions.explanation: Moi-moi is ground beans paste cooked in leaves or containers by steaming.

questions.topic: Preparation, Packaging and Marketing of Food
questions.stem: A drink made from tiger nuts is called
questions.explanation: Kunu aya is made by soaking, grinding and sieving tiger nuts.

questions.topic: Preparation, Packaging and Marketing of Food
questions.stem: The label on packaged snacks for sale should show
options: the seller's school report and the names of the people who cooked the snacks
only the price, as all other details are given by the shop that sells the snacks
the name, ingredients, production and expiry dates, and producer's address
the name of the buyer and the date on which the buyer promises to eat them
questions.explanation: A good label gives buyers the information they need to judge the product's safety and quality.

questions.topic: Preparation, Packaging and Marketing of Food
questions.stem: Giving buyers a free drink for every five meat pies they buy is an example of
questions.explanation: Promotion includes activities that attract buyers and increase sales.

questions.topic: Preparation, Packaging and Marketing of Food
questions.stem: Food vendors should obtain a medical certificate of fitness mainly because it
options: shows they are free from infectious diseases that could spread through food
is a type of advertisement that can be displayed to attract more customers
replaces the need for hygiene, since the vendor has been tested by a doctor
allows them to raise prices and sell their food in bigger and better shops
questions.explanation: Food handlers with infectious diseases can spread them through food, so regular medical checks protect the public.

questions.topic: Preparation, Packaging and Marketing of Food
questions.stem: A student sells zobo near the school gate where many people pass. This is an application of the marketing principle of
questions.explanation: Place refers to where and how the product is made available to buyers.

questions.topic: Preparation, Packaging and Marketing of Food
questions.stem: It cost a student ₦4,800 to make zobo. If she sells each bottle at ₦200, how many bottles must she sell to recover her cost?
questions.explanation: Number of bottles = ₦4,800 / ₦200 = 24 bottles.

questions.topic: Responsible Food Management
questions.stem: A food safety manager should train food handlers on
questions.explanation: Training food handlers in hygiene reduces the risk of food contamination.

questions.topic: Responsible Food Management
questions.stem: Kitchen waste in a restaurant should be
options: kept near the cooking pots for easy removal
kept in covered bins and emptied regularly
left open on the floor until closing time
thrown into the food store away from customers
questions.explanation: Covered bins keep away flies and rodents, which carry germs.

questions.topic: Responsible Food Management
questions.stem: A restaurant manager arranges regular pest control (fumigation) mainly to
options: reduce the price of food on the restaurant menu
make the food taste better by killing bad smells
keep rats, cockroaches and flies away from food
attract more customers who enjoy the chemical smell
questions.explanation: Pests carry germs and contaminate food, so controlling them protects customers.

questions.topic: Responsible Food Management
questions.stem: Cleaning chemicals in a kitchen should be stored
options: away from food in labelled containers
together with food in the same cupboard
questions.explanation: Keeping chemicals separate and clearly labelled prevents accidental contamination or poisoning.

questions.topic: Responsible Food Management
questions.stem: One effect of unhygienic food handling on the consumer is
options: improved trust in the restaurant and its staff
food-borne illness and loss of time and money
questions.explanation: Contaminated food causes illness, which leads to medical bills and time lost from school or work.

questions.topic: Responsible Food Management
questions.stem: A customer complains that food she bought tasted spoilt. The food safety manager should
options: serve the same food again to show that there is no problem
listen, investigate the complaint and correct the problem
ignore the complaint, as one customer cannot be correct
blame the customer for not eating the food while it was hot
questions.explanation: Handling complaints properly protects consumers and improves the safety of the food served.

questions.topic: Responsible Food Management
questions.stem: Labelling stored food with the date it was prepared or received helps to
options: make the food heavier and easier to stack on the shelves
know which food to use first and avoid serving spoilt food
increase the price of food kept for a long time in the store
hide the age of the food from the customers and the cooks
questions.explanation: Dates show how long food has been stored, so older food is used first and spoilt food is not served.

questions.topic: Responsible Food Management
questions.stem: Using older food stock before newer stock in a store is known as
questions.explanation: FIFO stock rotation ensures that food is used before it gets too old.

questions.topic: Responsible Food Management
questions.stem: In responsible food management, cooked food awaiting service should be kept
options: in direct sunlight so that it stays warm all the time
lukewarm for many hours so that it is ready to serve
very hot, or cold in a refrigerator, but not lukewarm
uncovered at room temperature so that it cools quickly
questions.explanation: Germs multiply fastest at warm temperatures, so food is kept hot or cold until it is served.

questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights
questions.stem:
(a) What is puberty? [2 marks]
(b) State two signs of puberty in boys and two signs in girls. [4 marks]
(c) Name two sexually transmitted infections and state two ways of preventing them. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Puberty is the stage of life when the body begins to mature sexually and changes from that of a child to that of an adult
1 mark: (b) Boys: deepening of the voice
1 mark: (b) Boys: growth of facial/pubic hair or broadening of the shoulders
1 mark: (b) Girls: development of breasts
1 mark: (b) Girls: beginning of menstruation or widening of the hips
1 mark: (c) STI 1, e.g. gonorrhoea, syphilis, HIV/AIDS, chlamydia
1 mark: (c) STI 2 (different from the first)
1 mark: (c) Abstinence from sexual activity
1 mark: (c) Avoid sharing sharp objects / use screened blood / seek early treatment
questions.explanation: Puberty brings physical changes in both sexes. STIs are prevented by abstinence and by avoiding contact with infected blood and sharp objects.

questions.topic: Family Needs, Goals and Standards
questions.stem:
(a) Differentiate between needs and wants, giving TWO examples of each. [4 marks]
(b) Explain short-term and long-term family goals with ONE example of each. [4 marks]
(c) State two ways in which needs, goals and standards are related. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Needs are things necessary for survival and well-being
1 mark: (a) Examples of needs, e.g. food, shelter, clothing, education
1 mark: (a) Wants are things desired but not necessary for survival
1 mark: (a) Examples of wants, e.g. jewellery, a big television, a car
1 mark: (b) Short-term goals are achieved within a short time (days or weeks)
1 mark: (b) Example, e.g. buying food for the week, paying a bill
1 mark: (b) Long-term goals take a long time (years) to achieve
1 mark: (b) Example, e.g. building a house, a child's university education
1 mark: (c) Needs give rise to goals
1 mark: (c) Standards are used to measure how well goals are achieved
questions.explanation: Needs are essential while wants are not. Goals may be short- or long-term, and standards help to judge whether goals that meet needs have been achieved.

questions.topic: Resources and Decision Making
questions.stem:
(a) Name two human and two non-human (material) resources of the family. [4 marks]
(b) List in order the steps in decision making. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Human resource 1, e.g. time, energy, knowledge, skills
1 mark: (a) Human resource 2
1 mark: (a) Material resource 1, e.g. money, land, house, equipment
1 mark: (a) Material resource 2
1 mark: (b) Identify the problem
1 mark: (b) Gather information about the problem
1 mark: (b) List the possible alternatives
1 mark: (b) Consider (weigh) the alternatives
1 mark: (b) Choose the best alternative and act on it
1 mark: (b) Evaluate the result of the decision
questions.explanation: Resources include personal qualities (human) and things (material). Decision making follows logical steps from identifying the problem to evaluating the result.

questions.topic: Consumer Challenges and Rights
questions.stem:
(a) Who is a consumer? [2 marks]
(b) State four rights of the consumer. [4 marks]
(c) Describe the procedure a consumer should follow to seek redress for a faulty product. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) A consumer is a person who buys and uses goods and services
1 mark: (b) Right to safety
1 mark: (b) Right to information
1 mark: (b) Right to choose
1 mark: (b) Right to be heard / redress / consumer education / basic needs / healthy environment
1 mark: (c) Keep the receipt and return the product to the seller to complain
1 mark: (c) If not settled, write to the manufacturer
1 mark: (c) Report to a consumer protection agency such as the FCCPC (or SON or NAFDAC as relevant)
1 mark: (c) As a last resort, take the matter to court
questions.explanation: Consumers have rights that protect them, and redress is sought step by step from the seller up to the courts.

questions.topic: Child Development and Care
questions.stem:
(a) Name four stages of child development in the correct order. [4 marks]
(b) State four factors that influence child development. [4 marks]
(c) Name four diseases that children are immunised against in Nigeria. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Prenatal stage
1 mark: (a) Infancy
1 mark: (a) Toddler stage
1 mark: (a) Pre-school (early childhood) stage, followed by school age
1 mark: (b) Heredity
1 mark: (b) Nutrition
1 mark: (b) Environment (home, community)
1 mark: (b) Health care / love and security / play
1 mark: (c) Tuberculosis (BCG)
1 mark: (c) Poliomyelitis (OPV)
1 mark: (c) Measles
1 mark: (c) Any other, e.g. diphtheria, whooping cough, tetanus, yellow fever, hepatitis B
questions.explanation: Child development follows stages and is shaped by heredity, nutrition, environment and care. Immunisation protects children from serious diseases.

questions.topic: Care of Family Clothing and Household Linen
questions.stem:
(a) Name four types of household linen and state where each is used. [4 marks]
(b) State three factors to consider when selecting household linen. [3 marks]
(c) Give three rules for storing clothes and household linen. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Bed linen, e.g. bed sheets, pillowcases (bedroom)
1 mark: (a) Table linen, e.g. tablecloths, napkins (dining)
1 mark: (a) Bathroom linen, e.g. towels
1 mark: (a) Kitchen linen, e.g. tea towels, oven gloves (accept curtains)
1 mark: (b) Durability
1 mark: (b) Ease of washing / colourfastness
1 mark: (b) Size, cost or absorbency
1 mark: (c) Store only clean and completely dry items
1 mark: (c) Store in clean, dry, airy places / use hangers for garments
1 mark: (c) Protect against insects (e.g. camphor) and check stored items regularly
questions.explanation: Linen is grouped by where it is used. Good selection and storage make linen last longer and stay clean.

questions.topic: Basic Pattern Drafting Techniques and Fashion Designing
questions.stem:
(a) Name four tools used in pattern drafting. [4 marks]
(b) State three rules for taking body measurements. [3 marks]
(c) Name three measurements needed to draft a basic skirt pattern. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Tape measure
1 mark: (a) Metre rule / ruler
1 mark: (a) French curve
1 mark: (a) Pattern paper, pencil, set square or tracing wheel
1 mark: (b) Take measurements over light clothing
1 mark: (b) Keep the tape neither too tight nor too loose
1 mark: (b) Record measurements immediately / tie a tape around the waist as a guide
1 mark: (c) Waist
1 mark: (c) Hips
1 mark: (c) Skirt length (waist to hem)
questions.explanation: Pattern drafting needs accurate tools and measurements. A basic skirt block uses waist, hip and length measurements.

questions.topic: Textiles: Properties, Production, Uses and Care
questions.stem:
(a) Define the following textile terms: (i) fibre (ii) yarn (iii) warp (iv) weft. [4 marks]
(b) Give two differences between natural and synthetic fibres, with ONE example of each. [4 marks]
(c) State four steps in laundering a cotton shirt. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a)(i) Fibre: a fine hair-like strand from which yarn is made
1 mark: (a)(ii) Yarn: fibres twisted together to form a continuous thread
1 mark: (a)(iii) Warp: lengthwise threads in a woven fabric
1 mark: (a)(iv) Weft: crosswise threads in a woven fabric
1 mark: (b) Natural fibres come from plants or animals; synthetic fibres are made from chemicals
1 mark: (b) Natural fibres are generally absorbent; synthetic fibres absorb little and dry quickly
1 mark: (b) Example of natural fibre, e.g. cotton, wool, silk, linen
1 mark: (b) Example of synthetic fibre, e.g. nylon, polyester, acrylic
1 mark: (c) Sort and soak
1 mark: (c) Wash in warm soapy water
1 mark: (c) Rinse thoroughly
1 mark: (c) Dry and iron with a hot iron
questions.explanation: Textile terms describe how fabric is made. Natural and synthetic fibres differ in source and properties, and laundering follows a set order.

questions.topic: Sewing Machine and Garment Construction Processes
questions.stem:
(a) Name four parts of a sewing machine and state the function of each. [8 marks]
(b) State four ways of caring for a sewing machine. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Needle
1 mark: (a) Carries the thread through the fabric
1 mark: (a) Presser foot
1 mark: (a) Holds the fabric in place while sewing
1 mark: (a) Bobbin
1 mark: (a) Holds the lower thread
1 mark: (a) Any other part, e.g. spool pin, feed dog, tension disc, stitch regulator, hand wheel
1 mark: (a) Its correct function
1 mark: (b) Clean off dust and lint regularly
1 mark: (b) Oil moving parts with sewing machine oil
1 mark: (b) Cover the machine when not in use
1 mark: (b) Use the correct needle and thread / repair faults promptly / store in a dry place
questions.explanation: Knowing the parts of a sewing machine and their functions helps in using it, while regular care keeps it working well.

questions.topic: Production of Cleaning Agents, Deodorants and Cosmetics
questions.stem:
(a) Name three home-made cleaning agents and state ONE use of each. [6 marks]
(b) State two roles of NAFDAC and SON in the control of cosmetics in Nigeria. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Cleaning agent 1, e.g. lime/lemon juice
1 mark: (a) Use, e.g. removing stains or cleaning brass
1 mark: (a) Cleaning agent 2, e.g. wood ash
1 mark: (a) Use, e.g. scouring pots
1 mark: (a) Cleaning agent 3, e.g. vinegar, baking soda, black soap or home-made polish
1 mark: (a) Its correct use
1 mark: (b) NAFDAC registers cosmetics and gives them registration numbers
1 mark: (b) NAFDAC tests products and removes unsafe or fake ones from the market
1 mark: (b) SON sets quality standards for products
1 mark: (b) SON inspects and certifies that products meet the standards
questions.explanation: Simple cleaning agents can be made from local materials. NAFDAC and SON protect consumers by regulating and setting standards for cosmetics.

questions.topic: Healthy Feeding and Eating Practice
questions.stem:
(a) State four healthy eating habits. [4 marks]
(b) What are food additives? Give two examples and their uses. [4 marks]
(c) State two effects of unhealthy feeding practices. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Washing hands before eating
1 mark: (a) Chewing food properly
1 mark: (a) Taking a small quantity at a time
1 mark: (a) Not talking with food in the mouth / eating at regular times
2 marks: (b) Food additives are substances added to food to preserve it or improve its colour, flavour or texture
1 mark: (b) Example 1 with use, e.g. salt as preservative or seasoning cube as flavour enhancer
1 mark: (b) Example 2 with use, e.g. food colouring, sugar in jam
1 mark: (c) Malnutrition, e.g. obesity or kwashiorkor
1 mark: (c) Diseases such as high blood pressure, diabetes or tooth decay
questions.explanation: Good eating habits support digestion and safety. Additives have uses but must be used correctly, and poor feeding leads to malnutrition and disease.

questions.topic: Food Purchasing, Processing, Preservation and Safety
questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between perishable and non-perishable foods, giving TWO examples of each. [4 marks]
(b) State two reasons for preserving food. [2 marks]
(c) Describe two methods of preserving fish. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Perishable foods spoil quickly
1 mark: (a) Examples, e.g. fresh fish, meat, milk, tomatoes
1 mark: (a) Non-perishable foods keep for a long time
1 mark: (a) Examples, e.g. dry rice, beans, garri, groundnut oil
1 mark: (b) To prevent spoilage and waste
1 mark: (b) To make food available out of season / to save money / ease of transport
2 marks: (c) Smoking: fish is placed on a rack over a fire so that heat and smoke dry it and slow spoilage
2 marks: (c) Salting, drying or freezing correctly described (e.g. salt draws out water; freezing slows germs)
questions.explanation: Perishable foods need preservation. Methods such as smoking, salting, drying and freezing remove water or slow micro-organisms.

questions.topic: Food Hygiene and Safety
questions.stem:
(a) What is food hygiene? [2 marks]
(b) State four ways of handling food safely. [4 marks]
(c) Name two micro-organisms that cause food spoilage and one sensory sign of spoilage for each. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Food hygiene is keeping food clean and safe from contamination at every stage from buying to eating
1 mark: (b) Wash hands with soap before handling food
1 mark: (b) Cover food to protect it from flies and dust
1 mark: (b) Keep raw and cooked foods apart
1 mark: (b) Store food at safe temperatures / use clean utensils
1 mark: (c) Moulds
1 mark: (c) Fluffy growth seen on bread or fruits
1 mark: (c) Bacteria (or yeasts)
1 mark: (c) Sour smell, slimy surface, or bubbles and sour taste for yeasts
questions.explanation: Hygiene protects food from contamination. Spoilage by moulds, bacteria and yeasts can be detected by sight, smell and taste.

questions.topic: Preparation, Packaging and Marketing of Food
questions.stem:
(a) Differentiate between a snack and a main meal. [2 marks]
(b) Name four snacks or drinks commonly sold in Nigeria. [4 marks]
(c) State four principles of marketing food. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) A snack is a light food eaten between main meals, while a main meal is a full meal eaten at regular mealtimes
1 mark: (b) e.g. puff-puff
1 mark: (b) e.g. chin-chin or plantain chips
1 mark: (b) e.g. zobo or kunu
1 mark: (b) e.g. meat pie, akara or moi-moi
1 mark: (c) Product: good quality, well packaged
1 mark: (c) Price: fair and covers cost
1 mark: (c) Place: sold where buyers are
1 mark: (c) Promotion: advertising to attract buyers
questions.explanation: Snacks are light foods between meals. Marketing food follows the principles of product, price, place and promotion.
